title: Stroop Interference Laboratory
summary: Six untimed practice trials, then 45 scored trials naming the ink colour of congruent, neutral and incongruent words. Results are withheld until the block ends, and the learner's own reaction times are then split into two effects measured from the neutral baseline: the cost of a conflicting word and the benefit of a matching one.
learningObjectives: Experience colour-word interference directly rather than reading about it.
Explain why a neutral condition is needed, and what is lost when only congruent and incongruent trials are compared.
Distinguish interference, the cost above the neutral baseline, from facilitation, the benefit below it.
Interpret a difference score as the distance between two condition means rather than as a property of a person.
Recognise how few trials, browser timing and a single participant limit what a block like this can establish.
interactionTypes: untimed practice block with per-trial feedback
scored block with all results withheld until it ends
one figure showing three condition means with both effects drawn from the neutral baseline
response cleaning reported rather than applied silently
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Reaction times are held in the page only and are gone when it is closed or reset.
accessibilityNotes: Every response is a full-size labelled key naming its colour in text, with the keyboard equivalent printed on the key; number keys 1 to 4 do the same job. No trial is ever timed out, so a learner may take as long as they need on any word. Nothing flashes, fades, moves or animates, so there is nothing for a reduced-motion setting to switch off. The task panel is dark and constant and every ink clears 7:1 against it. The results figure prints each mean beside its bar, names both effects with their values, and carries a description stating all three means and both effects; a data table gives every value including accuracy. The task does require telling four ink colours apart, which the page states before the learner starts.
dataStatus: The learner's own responses, computed in the browser and never stored. The stimuli are original: four colour words and eight common concrete nouns. No proprietary test material, published item set or normative data is reproduced.
simulationNotes: Interference is the mean incongruent reaction time minus the mean neutral reaction time; facilitation is the mean neutral minus the mean congruent. Correct responses only. Responses under 200 ms cannot be reactions to a four-choice display and responses over 3000 ms are lapses of a different kind; both are excluded from the means, counted, and reported on the page rather than dropped silently. Errors are excluded from the means and reported as accuracy. Fifteen scored trials per condition is enough to feel the effect and far too few to estimate anyone's reaction time; browser timing adds further noise, and a facilitation effect this small often fails to appear in a block this length. Trial order is randomised on every run, with no more than two consecutive trials sharing a correct response.
readmeTopic: colour-word interference, and why a neutral baseline turns one effect into two
